notes: The administrator is created on the first start from ADMIN_EMAIL (the admin email you enter) and ADMIN_PASSWORD (a generated password shown on the first-run card). TREK reads both only while its database has no users, so changing them later does nothing: change the password in TREK's settings instead.

One container, as in the official compose file: TREK keeps its SQLite database, logs and keys in /app/data and uploaded files (photos, documents, covers) in /app/uploads, one named volume each. The image starts as root only to fix the ownership of those two folders and then runs the server as the node user.

ENCRYPTION_KEY is a generated secret. TREK derives its at-rest keys from it with SHA-256 (API keys, MFA secrets, SMTP and OIDC passwords), so any string works and the same secret keeps old data readable after the container is recreated. TREK also copies it into /app/data/.encryption_key.

Behind the panel's HTTPS proxy, TRUST_PROXY=1 trusts exactly one hop, so TREK sees the forwarded https scheme and sets secure cookies (it does that by itself with NODE_ENV=production). FORCE_HTTPS is left off because the panel's web server already sends visitors to HTTPS, and the panel's health check talks plain HTTP on 127.0.0.1. APP_URL is the site's address (used for email links and OIDC); ALLOWED_ORIGINS is the same origin, for CORS.

The official compose file also sets read_only, cap_drop and no-new-privileges. Recipes cannot carry security_opt or capability changes, so those hardening options are not used; the container runs with Docker's default capabilities.

Place search asks TREK's own Places service (places.liketrek.com) by default, as upstream ships it. Set TREK_PLACES_ENABLED=false in the panel's environment editor to search OpenStreetMap instead and send nothing to that host.
